clips.send: Scorpius. The Scorpion of summer. The Scorpion is low in the south on summer evenings from Georgia. Its heart is Antares, a huge red supergiant. Its name means “rival of Mars” because of its red colour. Its long curving tail ends in a stinger.

clips.send: Polaris (North Star). Almost still, above Earth’s North Pole. Polaris sits less than 1° from the north celestial pole, the point in the sky that Earth’s axis points to. All night the other stars circle around it, while Polaris barely moves. Its height above the northern horizon equals your latitude: about 34° in Georgia, 40° in Beijing. It is about 430 light-years away.

clips.send: Canis Major (Sirius). Home of the brightest star at night. Contains Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky. Sirius looks so bright mainly because it is close: only 8.6 light-years away. Canis Major is Orion’s big hunting dog, following him across the winter sky.

clips.send: Canis Minor (Procyon). The Little Dog. Canis Minor is basically just two stars. Procyon is only 11.5 light-years away. Procyon, Sirius and Betelgeuse form the Winter Triangle.

clips.send: Taurus. The Bull with a red eye. The Bull, with the orange giant star Aldebaran as its eye. The V-shaped Hyades star cluster forms the bull’s face. The Pleiades (Seven Sisters) star cluster rides on the bull’s shoulder.

clips.send: Ursa Major (Big Dipper). The Great Bear, home of the Big Dipper. The seven bright stars of the Big Dipper are only part of the Great Bear constellation. The Big Dipper is an asterism: a famous star pattern that is not a whole constellation. From Georgia, the Dipper is high on spring evenings and low near the northern horizon on autumn evenings.

clips.send: Cassiopeia. The “W” near the North Star. Five bright stars make a “W” (or an “M”, depending on the time). It is on the opposite side of Polaris from the Big Dipper, so when one is low, the other is high. From Georgia, Cassiopeia is circumpolar: it never sets.

clips.send: Common mix-up: The Dipper’s stars are not all the same distance from us. Most are about 80 light-years away, but Dubhe is about 120.

clips.send: Aquila (Altair). The Eagle. The Eagle also flies along the Milky Way. Altair is the Cowherd in the Chinese Qixi story; the Milky Way separates him from Vega. Altair is only about 17 light-years away and spins very fast.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Polaris is NOT the brightest star in the sky (it is only about 48th). Sirius is the brightest. Polaris is famous because it does not move.

clips.send: Ursa Minor (Little Dipper). Polaris is at the end of its handle. Polaris is the last star in the handle of the Little Dipper. From Georgia the whole Little Dipper is circumpolar: it never sets. Most of its stars are faint. The brightest after Polaris is Kochab, an orange giant.

clips.send: Auriga (Capella). The Charioteer. A five-sided shape of stars high in the winter sky. Capella is really a pair of yellow giant stars. It is the sixth-brightest star at night. Auriga shares the star Elnath with Taurus in its outline.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Orion’s stars are not close together in space. Bellatrix is about 250 light-years away and Rigel about 860. They only look close from Earth.

clips.send: Pegasus. The Winged Horse of autumn. Pegasus is a sign of autumn evenings. Four stars make the Great Square of Pegasus (one corner, Alpheratz, officially belongs to Andromeda). The Square helps you find the Andromeda Galaxy, about 2.5 million light-years away: the most distant thing you can see with your eyes alone.

clips.send: Orion. The Hunter of the winter sky. The best-known winter constellation, seen in the south on winter evenings. Three stars in a row make Orion’s Belt. Red Betelgeuse marks a shoulder and blue-white Rigel a foot. Star colour shows temperature: red stars are cooler, blue stars are hotter. Orion sits on the celestial equator, so people almost everywhere on Earth can see it.

clips.send: Cygnus (Northern Cross). The Swan flying along the Milky Way. The Swan flies along the Milky Way. Its brightest stars form the Northern Cross. Deneb, its tail, is extremely powerful and very far away: around 2,600 light-years.

clips.send: 飞马座。秋季的飞马。飞马座是秋季夜晚的标志。四颗星组成“飞马座大四边形”（其中一角壁宿二其实属于仙女座）。顺着大四边形可以找到仙女座星系，它离我们约 250 万光年，是肉眼能看到的最遥远的天体。
clips.text: 飞马座. 秋季的飞马. 飞马座是秋季夜晚的标志。. 四颗星组成“飞马座大四边形”（其中一角壁宿二其实属于仙女座）。. 顺着大四边形可以找到仙女座星系，它离我们约 250 万光年，是肉眼能看到的最遥远的天体。

clips.send: 御夫座（五车二）。驾车的人。冬季高空中一个由星星组成的五边形。五车二其实是两颗黄色巨星组成的双星，是夜空中第六亮的恒星。御夫座的轮廓借用了金牛座的五车五。

clips.send: 北极星。几乎不动，位于地球北极的正上方。北极星离北天极（地轴在天空中指向的点）不到 1 度 。整夜其他星星都绕着它转，而北极星几乎不动。它在北方地平线以上的高度约等于当地的纬度：佐治亚州约 34 度 ，北京约 40 度 。它离我们大约 430 光年。

clips.send: 猎户座。冬季星空的猎人。最有名的冬季星座，冬天晚上出现在南方天空。三颗排成一排的星是“猎户腰带”（参宿一、二、三）。红色的参宿四是猎人的肩膀，蓝白色的参宿七是猎人的脚。恒星的颜色表示温度：红色较冷，蓝色较热。猎户座位于天赤道上，地球上几乎所有地方都能看到它。

clips.send: 天蝎座。夏季的蝎子。从佐治亚州看，夏天晚上天蝎座低低地挂在南方。蝎子的心脏是心宿二，一颗巨大的红超巨星，名字的意思是“火星的对手”，因为它也是红色的。长长弯曲的尾巴末端是毒刺。

clips.send: 金牛座。长着红眼睛的公牛。公牛的眼睛是橙色巨星毕宿五。V 字形的毕星团组成公牛的脸。昴星团（七姐妹星团）在公牛的肩膀上。

clips.send: 大熊座（北斗七星）。大熊，北斗七星就在其中。北斗七星只是大熊座的一部分。北斗七星属于“星群”：一个有名的星星图案，但不是一个完整的星座。从佐治亚州看，春天傍晚北斗高挂，秋天傍晚它低低地贴近北方地平线。

clips.send: 小熊座（小北斗）。北极星就在它的“勺柄”末端。北极星是小北斗勺柄末端的那颗星。从佐治亚州看，整个小熊座都是“拱极星座”，永远不会落到地平线以下。它的大多数星星都比较暗，除北极星外最亮的是橙色巨星“帝星”。

clips.send: 仙后座。北极星旁边的“W”。五颗亮星组成一个“W”（换个时间看就变成“M”）。它和北斗七星分别在北极星的两侧，一个低时另一个就高。从佐治亚州看，仙后座是拱极星座，永远不会落下。

clips.send: 天鹅座（北十字）。沿着银河飞翔的天鹅。天鹅沿着银河展翅飞翔。它最亮的几颗星组成“北十字”。天鹅的尾巴天津四发光能力极强，而且非常遥远，约 2,600 光年。

clips.send: 天鹰座（牛郎星）。雄鹰。天鹰座也在银河边飞翔。牛郎星（河鼓二）就是七夕故事里的牛郎，银河把他和织女隔开。牛郎星离我们只有约 17 光年，而且自转得非常快。

clips.send: 大犬座（天狼星）。夜空中最亮的恒星所在地。大犬座里有天狼星，它是夜空中最亮的恒星。天狼星看起来那么亮，主要是因为它离我们很近，只有 8.6 光年。大犬座是猎人的大猎犬，在冬季星空中跟着猎户座移动。

clips.send: 小犬座（南河三）。小猎犬。小犬座基本上只有两颗星。南河三离我们只有 11.5 光年。南河三、天狼星和参宿四组成“冬季大三角”。
